name: StageChip
summary: The one chip for a pipeline stage — Lead · Applied · Screen · Interview · Offer — used identically in the Today row, the application card, the Leads filter and the pipeline. Static by default; with onChange it becomes a cycling button (press or Shift+→ advances, Shift+← reverts) that confirms nothing and relies on the list's Undo toast. Rejected and Withdrawn are terminal: shown, never cycled, never red.

stage.intent: Controlled. The five pipeline stages cycle in that order; Rejected and Withdrawn are terminal states set from a menu elsewhere and render static whatever else is passed.

onChange.intent: Makes the chip a cycling <button>. Fires with the new and the previous stage; the app applies it at once, updates the pipeline count and shows the one Undo toast (backlog #10). Undo is the app passing the previous stage back.

isDisabled.intent: Cycling only: a stage the user may not change right now (e.g. while the agent is re-scoring). Stays visible and announced.

keyboard.action: Moves focus to / from a cycling chip. Static and terminal chips are never tab stops.
Advances to the next stage (onChange). At Offer it does nothing — the label says 'Final stage'; Offer never advances by accident.
Advances to the next stage, same as a press. Bound on the chip button itself — never on the row or the document, so it cannot fire inside an input.
Reverts to the previous stage. At Lead it does nothing. Plain arrows are left alone: they belong to the list (J/K) and to text fields.

a11y.name: Static: the stage text is the name ('Interview'). Cycling: aria-label 'Stage: Screen. Press to advance' — what it is and what pressing does; at Offer 'Stage: Offer. Final stage'.
a11y.announcements: A cycling chip announces a change by its own label changing (focus stays on it); the stage change itself is confirmed by the list's toast (role=status). No aria-live on the chip — two announcements for one change (Chip spec, rule 4). Emphasis (tint for Interview, strong for Offer) is decoration: the stage is always in the text.
a11y.targetSize: The pill is 28 px tall (size.target.sm, ADR-024) — above the 24 px AA minimum, inline in text rows; the row around it provides the 44 px touch context.

rules: One mapping everywhere (handoff): every stage quiet (border + secondary text), Interview tint, Offer strong — the single accent on the screen. The map is exported (stageEmphasis) and is the only place it lives; ActionRow, the card and the pipeline read it from here.

Terminal states are neutral: Rejected and Withdrawn render as quiet static chips, never danger colour (backlog 0c — rejection is a stage, not a failure) and never in the cycle. They are set from a menu, not by pressing the chip.
Cycling confirms nothing. onChange fires at once; the list shows the Undo toast and ticks the pipeline count. The chip never opens a dialog and never asks 'are you sure'.
Offer is final: pressing or Shift+→ at Offer does nothing and the label says so. Nothing wraps — a loop from Offer back to Lead would be the one stage change a user could make by accident.

Keys live on the button. Shift+→/← are handled by the chip's own keydown (Chip's onKeyDown passthrough for a cycling stage), so they work wherever the chip is rendered and never fire inside an input. Plain arrows are untouched.

The flip (motion spec 3): on a stage change the new label turns in on the Y axis from 90° to 0° over duration.normal — the half of the 240 ms flip that a remount can honour; the outgoing half is dropped rather than delaying onChange until an animation ends (ADR-034). Interruptible: a second change restarts it. Reduced motion: the token is 0, so the label simply swaps.
The chip never shows status colour (Chip spec, rule 3) and never carries the count — the pipeline count is the list's figure, updated after the change.
